origins: Fitness culture, medical anxiety, fashion, and sexual objectification tell us that our value is how our bodies look or perform. Illness, injury, aging, and weight changes can then feel like losses of worth, not merely of function.
teaches: God created humanity “in His own image,” which is true of every person and every body. Paul writes, “Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you…? You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.” The psalmist says, “All my days were written in Your book.” Paul adds, “Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.” Our bodies are gifts to steward, not measures of our worth.
self_statements: I am only as valuable as my body looks or performs.
If my body fails, I fail.
I am worth more when I am thin or fit.
errors: Equating myself with my body’s condition.
Seeing my body as perfect or worthless.
Demanding an ideal I cannot sustain.
Feeling dissatisfied and concluding that my worth is low.
questions: How have I linked my worth to my body, and where did I learn it?
What can my body do that I overlook?
What does it mean that I am made in God’s image?
What does it mean to steward a body, not worship or punish it?
How would I treat a friend’s body or illness?
What is one kind thing I can do for my body?
truth: My worth comes from being made in God’s image and bought at a price, not from how my body looks or performs. I can steward my body with care and thanks, whatever its condition.
hw_truths: I am made in God’s image.
My body is a temple of the Spirit.
I was bought at a price.
My days are written in God’s book.
My inner self is being renewed.
I can care for my body with kindness.
log: Each day, name one thing your body did for you and one thing that is true of you apart from your body.
actions: Write when you link your worth to your body.
List ten things your body lets you do.
Choose a gentle habit such as rest or a walk.
Say it on hard body days.
prayer: Lord, You made me in Your image and bought me at a price. Free me from measuring my worth by my body. Help me care for it with gratitude. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I link worth to my body?
What does image of God mean?
What would I tell a friend?
What kind thing can I do?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I was bought at a price, so my worth is not my body.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “My body determines my worth.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
